title: The Biggest Bet Of Century - Anthropic  - 9000% Growth At $1.2Tn Valuation Justified? - Rahul Jain
creator: Rahul Jain
source_note: Detailed summary generated from the video's English auto-captions; figures are as Rahul states them on screen (auto-captions garble some names, e.g. 'Ashwad Damoduran' for Aswath Damodaran, 'entropic' for Anthropic, 'clots' for Claude).
summary: Rahul Jain dissects Anthropic's record-breaking IPO — the world's largest ever, raising ~$81bn at $83 per share and valuing the company at ~$1.5tn fully diluted — and asks whether that valuation is justified. He traces the sprint from ~$380bn (Feb 2026, Series G) to ~$965bn (May, Series H) to $1.5tn at IPO, noting private investors captured most of the gain, and that the stock opened at ~$111, touched $115, closed at ~$97, and had fallen back to ~$81 by 24 Nov. He walks through Aswath Damodaran's model ($77/share intrinsic value, built on Anthropic reaching $1tn of annual revenue in 10 years) but cautions that Damodaran's valuations have often diverged sharply from market prices (Zomato, Paytm, Nvidia, Tesla). The fundamentals, he argues, are remarkable: revenue grew from $41m in FY23 to ~$35bn trailing-twelve-months in 2026 (+9,040%), with 11,900 enterprise customers spending $100k+ (up from 1,500 in Dec 2025), and Claude holds ~30% of the AI coding market. The $104bn nine-month loss is mostly a non-cash $94bn fair-value charge on convertible notes; operating cash flow is positive at ~$6.5bn and compute costs have fallen to ~53-56% of revenue. Risks: ~$900bn of compute commitments through 2045, open-source competition (notably from China), a 180/365-day lock-in with ~15bn Class A shares set to unlock, AI safety and regulation headlines, and extreme volatility. He gives no buy or sell recommendation, stresses tracking quarterly revenue growth, keeping AI allocations limited, and not fearing volatility if you play the theme.
